question: Should the first readiness release expose `api.registerReadinessCriterion` and operator-selectable plugin criteria as a supported Plugin SDK and configuration contract, or should plugin registration be deferred while core-only observations land first?
rationale: This choice defines a durable external plugin and configuration compatibility boundary; code review cannot determine whether maintainers want to support that API in this release.

options.title: Accept the public plugin contract
options.body: Sponsor the exported plugin criterion API and require exact-head compatibility and live runtime proof before landing this dependent layer.

options.title: Defer plugin registration
options.body: Keep readiness limited to core-owned conditions for now and split or close the plugin-facing API portion until a later supported SDK decision.

recommendation.title: Accept the public plugin contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor the exported plugin criterion API and require exact-head compatibility and live runtime proof before landing this dependent layer.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the linked readiness proposals and can clarify the intended contract, while a repository decision-maker must sponsor the final product direction.
